At Samaria about 87 to 95 percent of the sun was covered, in mid-morning (around 10 local time), not at noon; totality fell in Assyria. Six other eclipses covered half the sun or more at Samaria in the same reign, the 784 BC eclipse is also proposed, and some commentators read the verse as imagery, not an eclipse.

A partial eclipse dims the light but does not move a shadow back, and no published calculation shows that it would.
